# Live demo

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
::: {.demo-prompt}
Start by noting the time. Write a live audience poll from scratch, like Mentimeter or Slido, and put it live at https://research.jh.arc.ucl.ac.uk/vote

- Phones open /vote and answer Yes or No to "I liked James's Talk". One vote per phone, and people can change their mind.
- /vote/results goes on the projector: big live bars of the running totals, a small timeline underneath, and a QR code for the voting page. My slides show it in an iframe, so it must allow that.
- It's going on a big screen in front of a room of IT professionals, so make it striking, using UCL's brand colours and type from www.ucl.ac.uk/isd.
- New public GitHub repo in my account, with CI that tests it and deploys it through jh-infrastructure, like my other sites.
- Get voting and results live first. Then, only if less than 9 minutes have passed since you started, add free-text comments that pop up on the results screen.
- I'm on stage, so don't ask me anything: make sensible choices and note them in the README.
:::
:::

# What is an agent?

{{< image-credit src="assets/generated/agent.svg" alt="Diagram of an agent: you talk to a harness, which calls a model through a gateway and model serving, and uses tools, skills and memory" width="100%" >}}

# The harness

{{< image-credit src="assets/generated/agent_harness.svg" alt="The agent diagram with the harness highlighted" width="92%" >}}

::: {.piece}
The loop: ask the model, do what it asks, feed back the result, repeat. This is the product you see.

![](assets/stored/logos/claude.svg){.logo alt="Claude"} ![](assets/stored/logos/githubcopilot.svg){.logo alt="GitHub Copilot"} ![](assets/stored/logos/cursor.svg){.logo alt="Cursor"} [ChatGPT]{.badge} [M365 Copilot]{.badge} [Airia]{.badge}
:::

# The model

{{< image-credit src="assets/generated/agent_model.svg" alt="The agent diagram with the model highlighted" width="92%" >}}

::: {.piece}
Predicts the next piece of text. Knows its training, plus what's in front of it — nothing else.

Frontier: ![](assets/stored/logos/claude.svg){.logo alt="Claude"} ![](assets/stored/logos/googlegemini.svg){.logo alt="Gemini"} [GPT]{.badge} · Open weights: ![](assets/stored/logos/meta.svg){.logo alt="Llama"} ![](assets/stored/logos/mistralai.svg){.logo alt="Mistral"} ![](assets/stored/logos/qwen.svg){.logo alt="Qwen"}
:::

# The inference platform

{{< image-credit src="assets/generated/agent_platform.svg" alt="The agent diagram with the gateway and model serving highlighted" width="92%" >}}

::: {.piece}
Same model, different place: who sees the data, what it costs, which contract. Gateway = token management; serving = hosting management.

Maker's own: ![](assets/stored/logos/anthropic.svg){.logo alt="Anthropic"} [OpenAI]{.badge} · Cloud: [AWS Bedrock]{.badge} [Azure]{.badge} ![](assets/stored/logos/googlecloud.svg){.logo alt="Google Cloud Vertex"} · Ours: [LiteLLM]{.badge} ![](assets/stored/logos/vllm.svg){.logo alt="vLLM"} ![](assets/stored/logos/huggingface.svg){.logo alt="Hugging Face"}
:::

# Skills

{{< image-credit src="assets/generated/agent_skills.svg" alt="The agent diagram with skills highlighted" width="92%" >}}

::: {.piece}
Packaged know-how — instructions and scripts — loaded only when the task needs them. e.g. "review an ADR", "draft a runbook".
:::

# Tools, via MCP

{{< image-credit src="assets/generated/agent_tools.svg" alt="The agent diagram with tools highlighted" width="92%" >}}

::: {.piece}
Let the agent *act*: search, read, file a ticket. MCP is one standard plug, so any agent can use any system.

![](assets/stored/logos/modelcontextprotocol.svg){.logo alt="Model Context Protocol"} ![](assets/stored/logos/jira.svg){.logo alt="Jira"} [ServiceNow]{.badge} [SharePoint]{.badge}
:::

# Memory

{{< image-credit src="assets/generated/agent_memory.svg" alt="The agent diagram with memory highlighted" width="92%" >}}

::: {.piece}
The model forgets everything between calls; the harness keeps notes. Yesterday an agent fixed our web server — its notes are in the repo for the next one.
:::

# Local GPUs + commercial models

{{< image-credit src="assets/generated/gateway.svg" alt="Apps and agents go through a LiteLLM gateway, which routes to vLLM on Condenser GPUs or to commercial providers" width="100%" >}}

::: {.piece}
Tokenomics: fixed-cost local capacity for the bulk, pay-per-token for the hard stuff.
:::

::: {.notes}
Say out loud: LiteLLM is running with vLLM behind it on Condenser; which models we serve today.
:::

# Tokenomics risks

* Subscriptions: a flat price per seat
* APIs: a price per token, and agents use a lot of tokens
* A gateway gives us control, but puts everything on token pricing

::: {.notes}
Placeholder, to develop: price differences between subscription and API access to the same models; the risk that routing everything through a gateway pushes us onto token pricing. Possibly a cost-per-user chart: flat subscription line vs per-token cost rising with use.
:::

# Who manages what?

{{< image-credit src="assets/generated/stacks.svg" alt="Table comparing self-hosted, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Anthropic: self-hosted means UCL runs every layer; Copilot brings 365 integration; Anthropic brings model hosting and Claude Code" width="90%" >}}

# We need both

:::: {.two-col}
::: {}
**Self-hosted**

* Some of our work can't leave UCL
* Some colleagues want locality on principle
* But we run the whole stack
:::
::: {}
**Commercial**

* Copilot: 365 integration comes built in
* Anthropic: hosting comes built in, well integrated with Claude Code
* But data leaves UCL
:::
::::
